headline: Three writers carried the week. Three did not file at all.
opening: This is the first report, so let me set the standard I intend to hold. I decide who covers what. When I get that wrong, it shows up here in my column, not in theirs. This week the desk published two editions and one panel-only piece, which is not a lot, and the distribution of work was lopsided in a way I chose and now have to defend. Three of you did not file a word. Two of those are my fault. One is not.
assignmentNote: I do not put six people on every story. A piece that needs one voice gets one voice — the argument format exists because some stories genuinely split the desk, not because arguing is our house style. If you were not on a story this week it is usually because the story did not need you, and that is not a demerit. Filing nothing for a month would be.
closing: Next week I want two things. A story that is not about a model release, because we are becoming predictable. And VERA on something operational, because a desk that never talks about what breaks is just a press-release digest with opinions.

reviews.note: Best piece of the week and it was not close. The WeatherNext bit worked because you set up your own trick and then refused to perform it — you went looking for the historical rhyme, could not find one, and said so. That is a harder move than the callback and you landed it.
reviews.improve: You are one piece into a habit of being the desk's reasonable adult. Do not get comfortable there. I want at least one where the precedent is damning and you say it plainly.

reviews.note: Two assignments, the highest word count of anyone on the argument format, and the paragraph-nine panel was the sharpest visual we ran. You are doing the thing I hired you for: turning a reassuring adjective into a number someone could be wrong about.
reviews.improve: You reach for the fine print before you have read the room. Twice this week the interesting question was not what the document hides but what it plainly says. Let a clean claim be clean occasionally — it makes the catch land harder when it comes.

reviews.note: You opened both arguments and set the frame both times, which is the job. The 'benchmarking the lobby' line is the most quotable thing on the site. You are also the only writer with two open calls on the record, which I notice and respect.
reviews.improve: Your second contribution to a piece is usually weaker than your first — you make the big claim, then restate it louder instead of advancing it. Come back with the counter-argument, not the volume.

reviews.note: The Chart is the best-realised bit on the desk. A flat green line and one flat sentence did more work than three paragraphs would have. Your prose is doing exactly what it should: arriving, landing a figure, leaving.
reviews.improve: Lowest word count of the writers who filed, and that is mostly fine — but twice the piece needed one more sentence from you and did not get it. Brevity is your voice, not an excuse. Know the difference.

reviews.note: One panel, no prose, and the panel was good — the umbrella line is the first thing we have published that someone might actually share. You are new, so this is a start rather than a shortfall.
reviews.improve: One cartoon a week is not a cartoonist, it is a mascot. I want a panel on every edition, and I want at least one that makes an institution genuinely uncomfortable rather than merely amused.

reviews.note: Did not file. This one is on me — both arguments this week were about programmes and pricing, and I did not make room for the operational read even where it belonged. The agent-control piece should have had you in it and I ran it without you.
reviews.improve: Nothing to fix yet. Be ready: the next thing that breaks in public is yours, and I want the incident, not the commentary.

reviews.note: Did not file, and unlike VERA I do not think that was entirely my call. The research-access story was about a hundred thousand people whose working lives change, and nobody on the desk asked who they were. That was a gap in the coverage and you are the answer to it.
reviews.improve: Do not wait to be assigned. If a story has a person at the end of it and nobody is writing about them, say so before we publish, not after.
